fixes.explanation: Not quite, friend. In the dream, the thin cows don't run from anybody. Genesis 41:4 says the sickly, thin cows “…devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.” The skinny ones come up from the Nile and eat the fat ones. I'd have been reaching for the nearest pillow too, because that is NOT how cows work.

Rested sounds lovely, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt, did fall back asleep between the dreams (Genesis 41:5). But what the text says about his morning is “In the morning his spirit was troubled…” (Genesis 41:8). Rested isn't the word it uses. Then he summons the magicians and wise men of Egypt.

The captain of the guard does come up later in the passage. The cupbearer says the young Hebrew was a servant of the captain of the guard (Genesis 41:12). But the ones Pharaoh, king of Egypt, summons are “…all the magicians and wise men of Egypt.” (Genesis 41:8). Different crowd.

Pharaoh, king of Egypt, says the opposite, friend. After the thin cows devoured the well-fed ones, “…no one could tell that they had done so; their appearance was as ugly as it had been before.” (Genesis 41:21). Not one bit of difference. He tells this to Joseph, the young Hebrew, right before he says he woke up.

That's right. Joseph says the abundance “…will be forgotten…” and “…will not be remembered…” once the famine arrives (Genesis 41:30-31). He says the famine will be that severe. I think this one is heavy, so it's good that Joseph doesn't stop there. He goes on to say what Pharaoh can do to prepare.
